symbols.name: \(U\)
symbols.def: Common latent factor that may affect treatment and the response-type distribution.

symbols.name: \(\mu_a\)
symbols.def: Observed arm risk \(\mu_a=P(Y=1\mid A=a)\), defined whenever \(P(A=a)>0\).

symbols.name: \(Q\)
symbols.space: \(\mathcal P(\mathcal A\times\mathcal Y^3\times\mathcal U)\) for some finite \(\mathcal U\)

symbols.name: \(\widetilde P\)
symbols.def: Auxiliary product-mixture extension used to define observed common entropy.

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak M_\kappa(P)\)
symbols.def: Factual-compatible common-latent model fiber defined in \(\texttt{def:model-fiber}\).

symbols.name: \(\Theta_\kappa(P)\)
symbols.def: Sharp joint benefit--harm set defined in \(\texttt{def:identified-set}\).

symbols.name: \(\theta=(B,H)\)
symbols.def: Generic benefit--harm point with coordinates evaluated by \((B(Q),H(Q))\) under a causal law.

symbols.name: \(\theta_0\)
symbols.def: A point in the zero-budget star kernel.

symbols.name: \(\Phi_m\)
symbols.def: Benefit--harm projection \(\Phi_m(\pi,e,r)=(\sum_u\pi_u r_{01\mid u},\sum_u\pi_u r_{10\mid u})\).

symbols.name: \(G_P(A;Y)\)
symbols.def: One-shot common entropy of the observed binary pair, defined by an infimum over every finite auxiliary alphabet in \(\texttt{def:common-entropy}\); for binary \(A\) and \(Y\), the support-three cardinality bound makes this infimum a minimum.

symbols.name: \(\theta_c(P)\)
symbols.def: Midpoint of the zero-budget Fréchet segment \(\mathcal S_0(P)\).

symbols.def: Hausdorff metric induced by the Euclidean norm.

symbols.def: Candidate four-cell factual law in multinomial inversion.

symbols.def: Multinomial likelihood mass on the closed simplex, \(L_q(c)=N!\prod_{a,y}q_{ay}^{c_{ay}}/\prod_{a,y}c_{ay}!\), with the convention \(0^0=1\).

symbols.name: \(u(q,\alpha)\)
symbols.def: Largest likelihood level whose upper level set has \(q\)-probability at least \(1-\alpha\).

standard.name: Observed-law compatibility for a discrete SCM
Latent conditional exchangeability in the common-cause SCM

definitions.name: Common-entropy SCM fiber
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak M_\kappa(P)=\left\{Q:Q_{A,Y}=P,\ Y=Y(A)\ Q\text{-a.s.},\ A\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid U,\ U\text{ finite},\ \operatorname{Ent}_Q(U)\leq\kappa\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Finite latent-factor program
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal F_{m,\kappa}(P)=\left\{(\pi,e,r):\pi\in\Delta_m,\ e\in[0,1]^m,\ r_{\cdot\cdot\mid u}\in\Delta_4,\ -\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u\log\pi_u\leq\kappa,\ p_{ay}=\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u e_u^a(1-e_u)^{1-a}\sum_{i,j=0}^1r_{ij\mid u}\mathbf 1\{(1-a)i+aj=y\}\text{ for all }a,y\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Observed common entropy
definitions.construction:
Let the auxiliary range over every finite alphabet. Define
\[
G_P(A;Y)=\inf_{\substack{m\geq1,\ \widetilde P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal A\times\mathcal Y\times\{1,\ldots,m\}):\\ \widetilde P_{A,Y}=P,\ A\perp_{\widetilde P}Y\mid U}}
\left\{-\sum_{u=1}^m\widetilde P(U=u)\log\widetilde P(U=u)\right\}.
\]
For binary \(A\) and \(Y\), the binary specialization of the finite-cardinality theorem permits the convention \(1\leq m\leq2\) without changing the value; the resulting finite union of compact feasible sets attains the infimum, so \(G_P(A;Y)\) is a minimum. Zero-mass auxiliary states are allowed, with \(0\log0=0\).

definitions.name: BH-CERT construction handle
definitions.construction: Start from the three-state factor program, stratify the latent simplex by its support faces, use the continuous extension \(x\mapsto-x\log x\) with value zero at \(x=0\), propagate convergent interval enclosures through the factual and benefit--harm maps, use the star-kernel homotopy for certified inner fans, and use rigorous positive lower bounds on the constrained feasibility residual for exclusion. The construction must determine the subdivision, witness sections, and separation certificates rather than presuppose them.

definitions.name: Exact multinomial region
definitions.construction: For every candidate cell vector \(q\) in the closed simplex \(\Delta_4=\{q\in[0,1]^4:\sum_{a,y}q_{ay}=1\}\), define \(L_q(c)=N!\prod_{a,y}q_{ay}^{c_{ay}}/\prod_{a,y}c_{ay}!\) with \(0^0=1\), including zero-count and zero-cell boundary cases. Let \(u(q,\alpha)=\sup\{u:\sum_{c:L_q(c)\geq u}L_q(c)\geq1-\alpha\}\). Define \[\mathcal C_{N,\alpha}(C_N)=\{q\in\Delta_4:L_q(C_N)\geq u(q,\alpha)\}.\]

definitions.name: Regular-versus-contact inference handle
definitions.construction: Use the star-kernel theorem to represent the set by radial reaches from \(\theta_c(P)\), analyze \((P,\kappa)\mapsto\rho_\kappa(v;P)\) through the KKT strata of the three-state factor program, retain zero-mass strata, and estimate its directional derivative before reconstructing the set in Hausdorff metric. The analysis must derive the normalization and limit on regular, active-entropy, and support-changing strata.

statements.statement: For every \(m\geq1\), the image \(\Phi_m(\mathcal F_{m,\kappa}(P))\) is exactly the set of benefit--harm pairs generated by laws in \(\mathfrak M_\kappa(P)\) whose latent factor has at most \(m\) states. Consequently, \(\Theta_\kappa(P)=\bigcup_{m\geq1}\Phi_m(\mathcal F_{m,\kappa}(P))\), and both directions are constructive.
statements.justification: This lemma makes sharpness causal: every numerical factor is completed to an SCM, and every admissible SCM is represented by the program.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 gives a general response-function polynomialization, while JiangWeiKocaoglu2023 uses mutual-information consequences; neither gives this exact Shannon-entropy factor fiber for the joint cross-world coordinates.
statements.consumer: The equivalence is the soundness contract for every subsequent geometric statement and for BH-CERT witnesses.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(R=(Y(0),Y(1))\).  The technique is direct finite-kernel factorization: we prove the two inclusions by explicit constructions.

First let \(Q\in\mathfrak M_\kappa(P)\) and suppose that the support of \(U\) has size at most \(m\).  Relabel its positive-mass states by a subset of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), pad with zero-mass states if necessary, and define, for every positive-mass state,
\[
 \pi_u=Q(U=u),\qquad e_u=Q(A=1\mid U=u),\qquad
 r_{ij\mid u}=Q(R=(i,j)\mid U=u).
\]
At a zero-mass state choose \(e_u\in[0,1]\) and \(r_{\cdot\cdot\mid u}\in\Delta_4\) arbitrarily.  Conditional exchangeability, namely \(\texttt{ass:latent-exchangeability}\), gives, for every positive-mass state,
\[
 Q(A=a,R=(i,j),U=u)
 =\pi_u e_u^a(1-e_u)^{1-a}r_{ij\mid u}.
\]
By consistency \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\) and factual compatibility \(\texttt{ass:factual-compatibility}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 p_{ay}
 &=Q(A=a,Y=y)\\
 &=\sum_{u=1}^m\sum_{i,j=0}^1
 \pi_u e_u^a(1-e_u)^{1-a}r_{ij\mid u}
 \mathbf 1\{(1-a)i+aj=y\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, the entropy restriction \(\texttt{ass:entropy-budget}\) is exactly
\[
 -\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u\log\pi_u=\operatorname{Ent}_Q(U)\leq\kappa,
\]
with the stipulated convention at zero.  Hence \((\pi,e,r)\in\mathcal F_{m,\kappa}(P)\).  Direct summation also gives
\[
 B(Q)=\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u r_{01\mid u},\qquad
 H(Q)=\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u r_{10\mid u},
\]
so the pair generated by \(Q\) is \(\Phi_m(\pi,e,r)\).

Conversely, let \((\pi,e,r)\in\mathcal F_{m,\kappa}(P)\).  On the finite space \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), put
\[
 Q\{U=u,A=a,R=(i,j)\}
 =\pi_u e_u^a(1-e_u)^{1-a}r_{ij\mid u},
\]
and define \(Y=(1-A)Y(0)+AY(1)\).  The displayed masses are nonnegative and sum to one.  Their factorization proves \(A\perp R\mid U\), the definition of \(Y\) proves consistency, and the factual equations in \(\texttt{def:finite-factor-program}\) prove \(Q_{A,Y}=P\).  The entropy is \(-\sum_u\pi_u\log\pi_u\leq\kappa\), and the two response-type sums are precisely \(\Phi_m(\pi,e,r)\).  Thus \(Q\in\mathfrak M_\kappa(P)\) and realizes the proposed pair.  Taking the union over all finite \(m\), as required by \(\texttt{def:model-fiber}\) and \(\texttt{def:identified-set}\), proves the final equality and the asserted constructive equivalence.

statements.statement: For every binary observed law \(P\) and every \(\kappa\in[0,\log2]\), \[\Theta_\kappa(P)=\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa}(P)).\] Thus every feasible \((B,H)\) has a factual-compatible causal witness with at most three latent states and no larger Shannon entropy.
statements.justification: A support-three theorem converts an infinite union of nonconvex programs into one fixed-dimensional sharp representation.
statements.gap: KumarLiElGamal2014 supplies finite attainment and the general support bound for an exact common-entropy factor of a fixed finite joint law. The theorem's added step is to apply that result to the fixed joint law of treatment and the four-valued response type, then prove that preserving this joint law preserves all factual cells and both benefit--harm coordinates. Zhang2024 instead conditions on a specified full marginal law \(P(U)\), and DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 gives a larger generic response-function support architecture.
statements.consumer: A fixed three-state domain makes exact set inversion feasible and supplies a computational contrast with causaloptim's linear response-function workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a binary observed law \(P\), a budget \(\kappa\in[0,\log 2]\), and
\(\theta\in\Theta_\kappa(P)\).  The first technique is exact finite-mixture
compression at a fixed joint law.  By
\(\texttt{lem:factor-program-equivalence}\), there are an integer \(m\geq 1\)
and \((\pi,e,r)\in\mathcal F_{m,\kappa}(P)\) such that
\(\Phi_m(\pi,e,r)=\theta\).  Put
\[
 \mathcal R_0=\{0,1\}^2
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 J\bigl(a,(i,j)\bigr)
 =\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u e_u^a(1-e_u)^{1-a}r_{ij\mid u}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The right-hand side is nonnegative, and summing it over \(a,i,j\) gives
\[
 \sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u\{(1-e_u)+e_u\}
       \sum_{i,j=0}^1r_{ij\mid u}=\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u=1,
\]
so \(J\) is a probability mass function on
\(\mathcal A\times\mathcal R_0\).  Equation (1) itself supplies an extension
of \(J\) by the original state index: conditional on state \(u\), treatment
is Bernoulli with success probability \(e_u\), the response type has mass
function \(r_{\cdot\cdot\mid u}\), and the two variables are independent.
Its auxiliary entropy is
\[
 -\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u\log\pi_u\leq\kappa,
 \tag{2}
\]
where (2) is the entropy constraint in
\(\texttt{def:finite-factor-program}\).  Therefore, for the fixed joint law
\(J\),
\[
 G_J(A;R)\leq-\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u\log\pi_u\leq\kappa,
 \qquad R=(Y(0),Y(1)).
 \tag{3}
\]

Apply the published finite-alphabet common-entropy theorem recorded as
\(\texttt{lem:binary-common-entropy-cardinality}\) with
\(\mathcal X=\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal Z=\mathcal R_0\).  Since these
alphabets have sizes two and four, respectively, it gives an extension
\(\widetilde J\) of \(J\) by a finite variable \(W\) such that
\[
 A\perp_{\widetilde J}R\mid W,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Ent}_{\widetilde J}(W)=G_J(A;R),
 \qquad
 |\operatorname{supp}(W)|\leq 2^{\min\{2,4\}}-1=3.
 \tag{4}
\]
This is the only borrowed compression step.

Enumerate the positive-mass states in (4).  For each such state define
\[
 \pi'_w=\widetilde J(W=w),\qquad
 e'_w=\widetilde J(A=1\mid W=w),\qquad
 r'_{ij\mid w}=\widetilde J(R=(i,j)\mid W=w).
 \tag{5}
\]
All conditionals in (5) are taken only at states with \(\pi'_w>0\), so no
division by zero occurs.  If fewer than three states have positive mass, pad
the list with zero-mass states and choose their propensity and response
probabilities arbitrarily in the declared simplices.  The convention
\(0\log0=0\) makes the padded entropy equal to the entropy in (4).
Conditional independence in (4) and preservation of the \((A,R)\)-marginal
give, for every \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sum_w\pi'_w(e'_w)^a(1-e'_w)^{1-a}
   \sum_{i,j=0}^1r'_{ij\mid w}
      \mathbf 1\{(1-a)i+aj=y\}\\
 &\quad=\sum_{i,j=0}^1J\bigl(a,(i,j)\bigr)
      \mathbf 1\{(1-a)i+aj=y\}\\
 &\quad=\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u e_u^a(1-e_u)^{1-a}
   \sum_{i,j=0}^1r_{ij\mid u}
      \mathbf 1\{(1-a)i+aj=y\}
 =p_{ay}.
 \tag{6}
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus (6) verifies every factual cell, including when an observed treatment
arm has probability zero.  In particular, no treatment positivity or
arm-specific conditional risk is used.  Equations (3)--(5) also verify the
entropy constraint.

The second technique is preservation of linear marginals under fixed-joint
compression.  Summing (1) over \(a\) and using
\((1-e_u)+e_u=1\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_w\pi'_w r'_{01\mid w}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1J(a,(0,1))
 =\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u r_{01\mid u},\\
 \sum_w\pi'_w r'_{10\mid w}
 &=\sum_{a=0}^1J(a,(1,0))
 =\sum_{u=1}^m\pi_u r_{10\mid u}.
 \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]
By (5)--(7), the padded tuple belongs to
\(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa}(P)\) and its \(\Phi_3\)-image is \(\theta\).  Hence
\[
 \Theta_\kappa(P)\subseteq\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa}(P)).
 \tag{8}
\]
Conversely, \(\texttt{lem:factor-program-equivalence}\) constructs from every
tuple in \(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa}(P)\) a factual-compatible full-data law with
the same benefit--harm coordinates, conditional exchangeability given its
at-most-three-state factor, consistency, and no larger entropy.  Therefore
\[
 \Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa}(P))\subseteq\Theta_\kappa(P).
 \tag{9}
\]
Equations (8) and (9) prove the asserted equality and the stated constructive
witness conclusion for every binary observed law, including boundary laws.

statements.statement:
The no-individual-effect point obeys the exact equivalence
\[
(0,0)\in\Theta_\kappa(P)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G_P(A;Y)\leq\kappa.
\]
Here \(G_P(A;Y)\) optimizes over all finite auxiliary alphabets. When these equivalent conditions hold, its minimum is attained by an exact product-mixture factor with at most two positive latent states, and the explicit diagonal completion gives a causal witness \(Q\in\mathfrak M_\kappa(P)\) whose \(U\) also has at most two positive states and for which \(B(Q)=H(Q)=0\) and \(Y(0)=Y(1)\) almost surely. Conversely, every causal origin witness induces a feasible product-mixture factor with the same latent entropy.
statements.justification: The equivalence gives the exact entropy breakdown budget and constructively realizes the origin with at most two positive latent states.
statements.gap: Proposition 8 of KumarLiElGamal2014 supplies binary product-mixture compression, not the necessity map from a causal origin witness or the diagonal full-data completion proved here.
statements.consumer: The balanced contact test and BH-CERT origin face use the exact support-two witness rather than the full image's three-state domain.

statements.statement: For the balanced law \(P^\star\), using natural logarithms, \[I_{P^\star}(A;Y)=\log2-h(1/10)=0.368064\ldots<\kappa^\star=1/2<h(4/9)=0.686962\ldots=G_{P^\star}(A;Y).\] Hence the mutual-information origin test \(I_P(A;Y)\leq\kappa\) accepts \((0,0)\) at \((P^\star,\kappa^\star)\), whereas the exact common-entropy identified set excludes it. The strict inequalities persist on a relative neighborhood of \(P^\star\) in the positive binary-law simplex.
statements.justification: The full-support witness turns the strict information-measure gap into an exact exclusion of the no-effect causal point.
statements.gap: The proof derives the common entropy by a matching lower bound and two-component mixture, then uses lower semicontinuity to obtain a relative neighborhood rather than a single numerical example.
statements.consumer: Users can see exactly why the mutual-information rule fails the balanced early-kill test below the common-entropy contact budget.
statements.proof_tex:
The proof combines an exact conditional-moment lower bound with a matching product-mixture construction. Under \(P^\star\), both observed marginals are uniform and the crossover probability is \(1/10\). Direct substitution in the definition of mutual information gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{P^\star}(A;Y)
&=\frac9{10}\log\frac{9/20}{1/4}
  +\frac1{10}\log\frac{1/20}{1/4}\\
&=\frac9{10}\log\frac95+\frac1{10}\log\frac15
=\log2-h(1/10).
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]

We next derive the common entropy rather than creating its value by definition. Put \(X=(-1)^A\) and \(Z=(-1)^Y\). The balanced channel gives
\[
\mathbb E(X)=\mathbb E(Z)=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E(XZ)=P^\star(A=Y)-P^\star(A\neq Y)=\frac45.
\tag{2}
\]
Consider any finite exact product-mixture representation of \(P^\star\). Write \(\pi_u=P(U=u)\), \(x_u=\mathbb E(X\mid U=u)\), and \(z_u=\mathbb E(Z\mid U=u)\). Conditional independence and (2) imply
\[
\sum_u\pi_u x_u=0,
\qquad
\sum_u\pi_u z_u=0,
\qquad
\sum_u\pi_u x_uz_u=\frac45.
\tag{3}
\]
Fix a positive-mass state and write \(w=\pi_u\). Since \(|x_v|,|z_v|\leq1\), the two zero-mean equalities in (3) give
\[
w|x_u|
=\left|\sum_{v\neq u}\pi_vx_v\right|\leq1-w,
\qquad
w|z_u|
=\left|\sum_{v\neq u}\pi_vz_v\right|\leq1-w.
\tag{4}
\]
Using (4), the triangle inequality, and \(|x_vz_v|\leq1\),
\[
\frac45
\leq w|x_uz_u|+\sum_{v\neq u}\pi_v|x_vz_v|
\leq\frac{(1-w)^2}{w}+(1-w)
=\frac{1-w}{w}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus every atom obeys \(w\leq5/9\). Let \(q=\max_u\pi_u\). If \(q\leq1/2\), then
\[
\operatorname{Ent}(U)
=\sum_u\pi_u\log(1/\pi_u)
\geq\log(1/q)\geq\log2>h(4/9).
\tag{6}
\]
The last inequality is strict because \(h'(s)=\log((1-s)/s)\) changes sign only at \(s=1/2\), so \(h\) is uniquely maximized there.
If \(1/2\leq q\leq5/9\), group all states other than a maximizing atom. Writing their normalized masses as \(\bar\pi_v=\pi_v/(1-q)\), direct expansion of the entropy gives
\[
\operatorname{Ent}(U)
=h(q)+(1-q)\sum_{v\neq u_{\max}}\bar\pi_v\log(1/\bar\pi_v)
\geq h(q)\geq h(5/9)=h(4/9),
\tag{7}
\]
where nonnegativity gives the first inequality and \(h'(s)=\log((1-s)/s)\leq0\) on \([1/2,1]\) gives the second. Equations (6)--(7) prove \(G_{P^\star}(A;Y)\geq h(4/9)\) for every finite auxiliary.

For equality, take two auxiliary states with masses \(5/9\) and \(4/9\). In the first state let \(A\) and \(Y\) be independent Bernoulli variables with success probabilities \(1/10\); in the second state let \(A=Y=1\) deterministically. In the order \((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), the induced cell probabilities are
\[
\frac59\frac{81}{100}=\frac9{20},
\quad
\frac59\frac9{100}=\frac1{20},
\quad
\frac59\frac9{100}=\frac1{20},
\quad
\frac59\frac1{100}+\frac49=\frac9{20}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus (8) is a factual-compatible exact product mixture, and its auxiliary entropy is \(h(4/9)\). Together with (6)--(7),
\[
G_{P^\star}(A;Y)=h(4/9).
\tag{9}
\]

We certify the displayed decimals and strict inequalities without a floating-point premise. For \(x>0\), put \(z=(x-1)/(x+1)\), so \(|z|<1\). Integrating the finite geometric identity
\[
\frac1{1-t^2}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}t^{2k}+\frac{t^{2n+2}}{1-t^2}
\]
from \(0\) to \(z\) yields
\[
\log x=2\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{z^{2k+1}}{2k+1}+R_n,
\qquad
|R_n|\leq
\frac{2|z|^{2n+3}}{(2n+3)(1-z^2)}.
\tag{10}
\]
All quantities in the truncated sums and remainder bounds are rational for the rational arguments occurring in (1) and (9). Exact rational arithmetic with \(n=60\) gives
\[
0.3680642<I_{P^\star}(A;Y)<0.3680643<\frac12
<0.6869615<G_{P^\star}(A;Y)<0.6869617.
\tag{11}
\]
Therefore the six-decimal expansions in the claim and both strict inequalities follow.

It remains to prove neighborhood persistence. By \(\texttt{lem:binary-common-entropy-two-state}\), for every binary law the minimum defining common entropy is attained on the compact parameter space
\[
\Delta_2\times[0,1]^2\times[0,1]^2,
\tag{12}
\]
where the last two factors are the Bernoulli success probabilities of \(A\) and \(Y\) in each state. The product-mixture map and entropy, with \(0\log0=0\), are continuous.

Let \(P_n\to P\). Choose two-state minimizers for \(P_n\) and pass, along a subsequence attaining \(\liminf_nG_{P_n}(A;Y)\), to a convergent subsequence in (12). Continuity of the mixture map makes the limit feasible for \(P\), and continuity of entropy gives
\[
G_P(A;Y)\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}G_{P_n}(A;Y).
\tag{13}
\]
Hence \(G_P(A;Y)\) is lower semicontinuous. Mutual information is continuous on the finite positive-law simplex because it is a finite sum of continuous \(x\log x\) terms and the marginals stay positive. By (11), there is therefore a relative neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(P^\star\) in the positive binary-law simplex such that
\[
I_P(A;Y)<\frac12<G_P(A;Y)
\qquad(P\in\mathcal N).
\tag{14}
\]
At \((P^\star,\kappa^\star)\), and throughout \(\mathcal N\) at budget \(1/2\), the rule \(I_P(A;Y)\leq\kappa\) therefore accepts the origin. In contrast, \(\texttt{thm:origin-common-entropy-frontier}\) and (14) give \((0,0)\notin\Theta_{1/2}(P)\). This proves the claimed strict estimand-level false inclusion and its persistence.

statements.statement: Under treatment positivity, the sensitivity path has the exact endpoints \[\Theta_0(P)=\mathcal S_0(P),\qquad \Theta_\kappa(P)=\mathcal R(P)\quad\text{for every }\kappa\geq h(p_1).\] The first equality is attained by every Fréchet coupling of Bernoulli margins \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\); the second is attained by a witness with \(U=A\). In particular, the high-budget coordinate projections recover the sharp factual benefit and harm bounds.
statements.justification: These reductions anchor the new sensitivity set to randomized Fréchet geometry and unrestricted probability-of-causation bounds.
statements.gap: TianPearl2000 gives sharp scalar probability-of-causation bounds, and Pena2023 studies separate benefit and harm bounds. Neither identifies the full joint rectangle as the high-common-entropy limit or the zero-budget segment of one sensitivity path.
statements.consumer: The endpoint formulas provide exact regression tests for implementations and interpretable anchors for sensitivity plots.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta_\kappa(P)\), every \(\theta_0\in\mathcal S_0(P)\), and every \(t\in[0,1]\), \[(1-t)\theta_0+t\theta\in\Theta_\kappa(P).\] A witness is obtained without adjoining a mixture indicator: retain the latent masses and propensities of a witness for \(\theta\), and replace each latent-specific response-type law by its common convex mixture with one no-confounding response law attaining \(\theta_0\). Therefore \(\mathcal S_0(P)\) lies in the star kernel of \(\Theta_\kappa(P)\), and \(\Theta_\kappa(P)\) is path connected.
statements.justification: The theorem supplies global topology despite the nonconvex entropy sublevel set and avoids the entropy cost of an external mixture indicator.
statements.gap: Neither the scalar programs of JiangWeiKocaoglu2023 nor the coordinatewise bounds of Pena2023 address joint-set topology. Standard convex interpolation is unavailable because low Shannon entropy is a nonconvex constraint.
statements.consumer: The star kernel gives BH-CERT a certified inner-set generator and guarantees that sensitivity regions cannot split into disconnected islands.

statements.statement: Can the BH-CERT handle be completed on the balanced law \(P^\star\) with support at most three so that it finitely certifies exclusion of \((0,0)\) for every fixed \(\kappa<G_{P^\star}(A;Y)\), while its nested inner and outer complexes converge in Hausdorff distance at the contact budget \(\kappa=G_{P^\star}(A;Y)\), including boxes whose witness has a zero latent mass or active entropy equality? A valid construction may not assume an interval-Newton or Krawczyk rank condition.
statements.justification: This is the smallest singular instance that distinguishes genuine two-sided certification from regular-root numerics.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 certifies scalar polynomial bounds by primal--dual branch and bound, while ArayaReyes2016 surveys interval contractors. Neither closes entropy-contact boxes with changing support and exact causal witnesses.
statements.consumer: Failure of this test triggers a pivot before a general BH-CERT implementation is presented as complete.

statements.statement: For every \(P\), \(\kappa\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), can BH-CERT be constructed to terminate with \[K^-_\varepsilon(P,\kappa)\subseteq\Theta_\kappa(P)\subseteq K^+_\varepsilon(P,\kappa),\qquad d_{\mathrm H}(K^-_\varepsilon,K^+_\varepsilon)\leq\varepsilon,\] while attaching an exact SCM witness section to every included cell and a checkable positive feasibility-residual certificate to every excluded cell, including all zero-weight and entropy-contact strata, without a local rank assumption?
statements.justification: A sharp nonlinear identified set is operational only if both inclusion and exclusion are auditable at its singular boundary.
statements.gap: JonzonSachsGabriel2023 automates polyhedral symbolic bounds, AudetMessineNinin2022 certifies biobjective proximity, and FernandezGoth2009 constructs interval outer sets; no result supplies this two-sided causal-image contract for a Shannon-entropy factor model.
statements.consumer: The procedure would provide auditable computation for common-entropy benefit--harm regions and a computational contrast with causaloptim's polyhedral workflow.

statements.statement: Using the star-centered radial and KKT-stratified directional-derivative handle, what are the exact normalizations and weak limits of \(d_{\mathrm H}(\Theta_\kappa(\widehat P_N),\Theta_\kappa(P))\) at regular pairs, active-entropy pairs, and support-changing contact pairs, and which derivative-aware resampling rule is uniformly valid across those regimes? The answer must derive rather than assume the radial and set-valued expansions.
statements.justification: Entropy equality and disappearing latent masses create a phase transition that ordinary smooth set estimators do not capture.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 treats criterion-defined identified sets, FangSantos2019 treats directionally differentiable maps, and MastenPoirier2020 treats breakdown frontiers. None derives the Hausdorff law of this entropy-constrained causal image at support contact.
statements.consumer: The result would separate conservative exact finite-sample coverage from sharper large-sample uncertainty quantification at scientifically relevant breakdown budgets.

statements.statement: For every joint probability mass function \(J\) on a product of two nonempty finite alphabets \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\), define \[G_J(X;Z)=\inf_{\substack{\widetilde J_{X,Z}=J,\ W\text{ finite}:\\ X\perp_{\widetilde J}Z\mid W}}\operatorname{Ent}_{\widetilde J}(W).\] The infimum is attained, and an entropy-minimizing exact factor can be chosen so that \[|\operatorname{supp}(W)|\leq 2^{\min\{|\mathcal X|,|\mathcal Z|\}}-1.\]

source.locator: Section V, Proposition 6, with finite attainment justified by Proposition 5 and the remark following equation (1)
source.verbatim_statement: To compute \(G(X;Y)\) for a given pmf \(p_{XY}(x,y)\), it suffices to consider \(W\) with cardinality \(|\mathcal W|\leq 2^{\min(|\mathcal X|,|\mathcal Y|)}-1\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the source TeX of arXiv:1402.0062, Section V, Proposition 6. The paper defines common entropy by a minimum in equation (1), and the following remark uses the finite reduction of Proposition 5 to justify attainment.

statements.justification: The published theorem supplies the general finite-alphabet entropy-minimizing product-mixture compression used after the complete joint law of treatment and response type is fixed.
statements.gap: It does not itself perform the causal reconstruction or prove that preserving the fixed joint law preserves all factual and benefit--harm coordinates; those are the new steps in \(\texttt{thm:three-state-reduction}\).
statements.consumer: The exact origin frontier and the exact support-three representation of the full benefit--harm image.

statements.statement: Let \(J\) be any probability mass function on \(\{0,1\}^2\). Among all finite extensions of \(J\) satisfying \(X\perp Z\mid W\), the minimum of \(\operatorname{Ent}(W)\) is attained, and an entropy-minimizing exact product-mixture factor can be chosen with \(W\) having at most two positive-mass states.

source.locator: Equation (1) and the immediately following attainment remark; Proposition 5; Section V, Proposition 8 (source label \(\texttt{prop:2letter}\)); and Appendix G (source label \(\texttt{proof:2letter}\))
source.verbatim_statement: It considers all possible cases for \(W\) and finally concludes that \(|\mathcal W|=2\) suffices.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the source TeX of arXiv:1402.0062. Equation (1) defines common entropy by a minimum, the immediately following remark explains attainment via a finite cardinality reduction, Proposition 5 supplies finite attainment, Section V Proposition 8 gives the binary two-state conclusion, and Appendix G (source label \(\texttt{proof:2letter}\)) contains its detailed proof. The source macro for the alphabet of \(W\) is expanded to \(\mathcal W\); the wording and formula are otherwise unchanged.

statements.justification: This is the published binary specialization that supplies the support-two entropy minimizer used on the no-effect origin face.
statements.gap: The information-theoretic result does not construct potential outcomes or verify factual compatibility; those causal steps are proved in \(\texttt{thm:origin-common-entropy-frontier}\).
statements.consumer: The exact origin theorem uses this leaf to obtain both finite attainment and the two-positive-state support bound before performing the diagonal causal completion.

statements.statement: For the balanced reverse-channel witness \(P^\dagger\), benefit--harm point \(\theta^\dagger\), and entropy budget \(\kappa^\dagger\), one has \(0<\kappa^\dagger<\log2\) and \[\theta^\dagger\in\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger))\setminus\Phi_2(\mathcal F_{2,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)).\] Consequently, \[\Phi_2(\mathcal F_{2,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger))\subsetneq\Phi_3(\mathcal F_{3,\kappa^\dagger}(P^\dagger)),\] so three latent states are sometimes necessary for the full benefit--harm image.
statements.justification: The witness certifies that the general three-state reduction cannot be strengthened to two states over the full benefit--harm image.
statements.gap: The product-mixture support-pattern obstruction appears in KumarLiElGamal2014, Section V, Example 2 and Appendix A; the proposition proves the factual-compatible response-type embedding and its exact entropy budget.
statements.consumer: Together with the binary two-state origin-face result, it establishes the exact support-cardinality elbow: two states on the no-effect face and three states in the full image.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the four-cell factual law \(P(A,Y)\); the identification results are population statements, and the supporting confidence construction uses the exact multinomial experiment.
sampling_model.units: Each unit has fixed binary potential outcomes \(Y(0),Y(1)\) under a full-data law \(Q\) with a finite common latent factor \(U\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is observational and may be confounded, with \(A\perp(Y(0),Y(1))\mid U\).
sampling_model.overlap: The main geometric results impose only \(0<P(A=1)<1\); the analytic separation law \(P^\star\) has all four factual cells positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nonparametric nuisance functions. The observed nuisance is the four-cell probability vector, estimated by multinomial frequencies or covered by an exact likelihood-ordered region.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Common entropy is the minimum Shannon entropy over exact product-mixture factorizations, with finite cardinality bounds and a binary closed form.
Low latent entropy implies mutual-information constraints that yield computable outer bounds for scalar causal effects.
Observed factual probabilities give sharp unrestricted bounds for probabilities of causation, including benefit.
Separate benefit and harm bounds are derived from two sensitivity parameters or a measured proxy.
For discrete causal effects, closed-form partial-identification bounds are tight when the full marginal distribution \(P(U)\) of the unmeasured confounder is specified.
Sharp symbolic nonparametric bounds are derived for benefit and related functionals without a Shannon-entropy budget.
Discrete causal queries reduce to finite polynomial programs with continuously refined valid outer bounds and epsilon-sharp scalar guarantees.
The causaloptim workflow automates tight symbolic bounds for linear response-function problems by vertex enumeration.
Likelihood-ordered covering collections yield finite-sample multinomial confidence regions with controlled coverage.
Criterion-defined identified sets admit consistency, rate, and confidence-region analysis under regularity conditions.
Breakdown frontiers for treatment-effect conclusions admit root-sample estimators and derivative-aware uniform confidence bands.

tldr: Average effects conceal simultaneous benefit and harm, while existing low-entropy-confounding bounds replace the latent entropy restriction by mutual-information consequences and study scalar causal probabilities. The focal object is the exact joint set \(\Theta_\kappa(P)\) of benefit and harm over factual-compatible common-latent SCMs. The field-grade kernel is an exact three-state representation, an iff common-entropy threshold for entry of universal no-effect, a full-support law where the mutual-information relaxation admits that point too early, the zero-budget Fréchet segment and high-budget factual rectangle, and a star kernel for every intermediate budget. The principal open question is whether a singularity-aware BH-CERT construction can return nested Hausdorff-certified inner and outer complexes with exact causal witnesses and exclusion certificates. An imported exact multinomial coverage event yields whole-set coverage as a supporting set-mapping corollary, while the regular-versus-contact Hausdorff law remains a separate inference frontier.

project_justification.gap: JiangWeiKocaoglu2023 uses mutual-information consequences of low latent entropy for scalar causal bounds; Zhang2024 gives tight binary causal partial identification conditional on a specified full marginal law \(P(U)\); and Pena2023 and GabrielSachsJensen2024 bound benefit or harm without mapping their jointly attainable entropy-indexed plane. None treats an unknown \(U\) restricted only by \(\operatorname{Ent}_Q(U)\leq\kappa\) and identifies the joint cross-world plane. The response-function and interval literatures do not certify the image at zero latent masses or active entropy equality.
project_justification.niche: At the no-effect origin, exact feasibility is a common-entropy factorization problem rather than a mutual-information inequality. Away from the origin, factual compatibility, cross-world response types, and the nonconvex Shannon sublevel set jointly determine a new two-dimensional sharp object with singular support changes.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the exact causal factor program and its proposed three-state reduction, derives the sharp origin threshold and global star-kernel geometry, and subjects the computational claim to a balanced-channel early-kill test. Exact whole-set coverage is retained as the supporting deterministic image of an imported multinomial coverage event.

related_work: KumarLiElGamal2014 defines one-shot common entropy over arbitrary finite auxiliaries and proves the binary support-three reduction and closed-form results; the origin theorem adds the causal necessity and sufficiency map. KocaogluShakkottaiDimakisCaramanisVishwanath2020 uses common entropy to distinguish causal graphs and to modify constraint-based discovery, not to identify joint counterfactual benefit and harm. JiangWeiKocaoglu2023 motivates low-entropy confounding and derives scalar mutual-information programs; the strict-separation proposition identifies an open region where that relaxation admits the no-effect point before an exact latent can. JiangKocaoglu2024 develops graph-specific conditional common entropy for instrumental-variable testing and scalar partial identification, leaving this two-variable cross-world plane untreated. Zhang2024 gives closed-form tight binary causal partial identification when the full marginal law \(P(U)\) is specified; here \(U\) is unknown and only \(\operatorname{Ent}_Q(U)\leq\kappa\) is imposed, while the target is the joint cross-world benefit--harm set and its entropy-budget support reduction rather than scalar interventional effects. Zhang2024 therefore does not imply the three-state common-entropy theorem, and that theorem does not imply Zhang2024's bounds conditional on an arbitrary specified \(P(U)\). TianPearl2000 supplies the unrestricted probabilities-of-causation benchmark. Pena2023 and GabrielSachsJensen2024 establish the clinical importance and sharp bounding geometry of benefit and harm under different restrictions, but not their common-entropy joint set. SachsJonzonSjolanderGabriel2022 and DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 inform the response-function encoding and certified-bounding architecture. JonzonSachsGabriel2023 supplies causaloptim's polyhedral workflow as a computational point of contrast; BH-CERT targets a nonlinear entropy-constrained image and does not claim a class extension of causaloptim. ChafaiConcordet2009 supplies the exact multinomial coverage event on the closed simplex; whole-set coverage here is only its supporting deterministic image. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, FangSantos2019, and MastenPoirier2020 motivate, without settling, the separate regular and entropy-contact Hausdorff analysis.
technical_internal_limitation: The asserted support-three equality is not a corollary of the binary common-entropy theorem: KumarLiElGamal2014 reduces the pure binary product-mixture problem, whereas the present fiber must also preserve two cross-world coordinates and factual treatment-specific moments. BH-CERT is therefore conditioned on proving this new reduction, and the balanced-channel contact calculation is an explicit early-kill test rather than evidence of general termination.
honest_scope: The population threshold, endpoint, and star-kernel claims are separated from the unresolved computational and inference objects. BH-CERT termination at zero weights and active entropy equality is open, as is the exact regular-versus-contact Hausdorff law. Finite-sample whole-set coverage is a supporting corollary of the imported exact multinomial coverage event and does not claim a new confidence-region construction or optimal expected area. Under \(\kappa=0\), the proposal reduces to the known Fréchet coupling segment with \(B-H=\mu_1-\mu_0\); under \(\kappa\geq h(p_1)\), it reduces to the unrestricted factual benefit--harm rectangle.
